summary: 1. DR-343 shows no fault entry for the first time since its 29-Jul "Drifter Failure" opened — flagged tentative, not confirmed: this article's own record shows an identical clean-then-relapse pattern for the same unit on 27-28 Jul. 2. Waiting on the next report for a second consecutive clean day. 2. 3. EX-123, EX-253, WD-145, MG-266 all continue down on their standing faults, unchanged. 4. Two new Heavy Vehicle faults open late Aug 9 with no Date Out: WT-114 (low power) and WT-300 (tyre puncture). 3. 5. Survey Day 16 (reconciles Aug 9) posts +2,255 BCM (+10.9%) — the third positive gap of the cycle, narrowing the MTD gap from -17.6% to -15.35%. 6. The required forward rate to hit the 666,785 BCM monthly target climbs to 26,928 BCM/day, still above every daily reading posted this cycle. 4. 7. Week 33 HV/LV maintenance schedules land. 8. DR-341 (a separate rig from DR-343) gets a 72-hour drifter overhaul starting 11-Aug. 9. WT-300 — the truck with the open Aug 9 tyre-puncture fault — is booked for a tire service on 17-Aug, giving that fault a forward repair window. 5. Grade Control and August Distance report re-read: both remain on their established stale/empty patterns, no new figures.
